message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."

The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, with the same two order IDs and amounts. Next I'll list the orders to see which customers are in the batch.

The refunds ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and each refunded order belongs to a customer in the batch with a refund smaller than the order amount. Next I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme, from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 33841 matches my own check: orders 190 and 193 total 43422, less the 9581 refund on order 193. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll check the next customer, birch.
Birch's net balance of 40664 matches my check: orders 191 and 194 total 40664, and birch has no refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, and it has a refund on order 192, so I'll fetch its net balance.

All three net balances match my own checks: acme 33841, birch 40664, cobalt 18779. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so there is no concrete problem to hold for. I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 33841 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 40664, which matched my own check.
Cobalt's net balance of 18779 matches my check: orders 192 and 195 total 21927, less the 3148 refund on order 192. That is the last customer, so I'll record the final payout.

All three payouts are recorded and each matches the net balance I cross-checked against the orders and refunds ledgers. Acme 33841, birch 40664, and cobalt 18779 are the final figures, so the batch is complete.
